issue.title: Constraint inference: chained constraints can't revise a covariant binding
Strip all whitespace from the license key
issue.body:
Sub-issue of LuckyPennySoftware/AutoMapper#4659.

## Problem

A valid license key that contains whitespace fails with a misleading signature error:

```
Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens.SecurityTokenInvalidSignatureException: IDX10511: Signature validation failed. Keys tried: 'Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens.RsaSecurityKey, KeyId: 'LuckyPennySoftwareLicenseKey/bbb13acb59904d89b4cb1c85f088ccf9' ...
```

This happens often in practice:
- Resellers deliver keys inside PDFs, and PDF renderers insert newlines. Both confirmed newline cases in support came from PDF delivery.
- Email clients wrap the key across lines. In one case a reseller's email broke the signature after `-` characters.
- Kubernetes secrets created from files (`kubectl create secret --from-file`) and mounted secret files usually keep a trailing newline.
- Config files and environment variables pick up trailing spaces.

Online JWT decoders (jwt.io) quietly ignore the whitespace, so customers check the key there, see that it's valid, and report a bug.

| Key value | Result |
|---|---|
| valid key | OK |
| key + `\n` / `\r\n` / `" "` | IDX10511 |
| key with embedded line breaks | IDX10511 |

## Fix

In `src/MediatR/Licensing/LicenseAccessor.cs` (`ResolveLicenseKey`), remove **all** whitespace characters from each key source, not just leading and trailing ones. This applies to the explicit key(s), the product env var and `LUCKYPENNY_LICENSE_KEY`.

- This is safe: a license key is a JWS in compact form, which contains only base64url characters (`A-Z a-z 0-9 - _`) and `.`, so whitespace is never meaningful.
- A value that is empty after stripping counts as not set, so resolution falls through to the next source.
- Today MediatR already treats a whitespace-only value as not set (`IsNullOrWhiteSpace`), but it passes surrounding or embedded whitespace through unchanged.

## Tests

- Keys with a trailing `\n`, `\r\n`, space or tab, and with embedded line breaks, resolve to the clean key and validate.
- A whitespace-only explicit key falls back to the env vars.
- Whitespace in the env var values is stripped too.

issue.title: MediatR license key configuration
issue.body:
Currently delivering license key is possible either during MediatR services registration
```
services.AddAutoMapper(cfg => { cfg.LicenseKey = "key"; });
```
or by using mapper configuration directly
```
var config = new MapperConfiguration(cfg => { cfg.LicenseKey = "key"; }, loggerFactory);
var mapper = new Mapper(config);
```
of by setting one of the env variables
```
MEDIATR_LICENSE_KEY
LUCKYPENNY_LICENSE_KEY
```
The problem is that when license key is delivered by another service e.g.
```
public interface ILicenseKeyProvider {
  string GetMediatrLicense()
  string GetAutomapperLicense()
}
```
it is not possible to inject and use such service to configure license key. It would be nice to be able to do following
```
        services
            .AddOptions<MediatRServiceConfiguration>()
            .Configure<ILicenseKeyProvider>(
                (cfg, lp) => {
            cfg.LicenseKey = lp.GetMediatrLicense();
        });
```
Such approach would also open ```IConfigureOptions<MediatRServiceConfiguration>``` pattern. It's interesting that Automapper supports this approach already.

issue.title: Setting generic registration limits to 0 doesn't disable them
issue.body:
The XML docs for two of the generic handler registration limits on `MediatRServiceConfiguration` say "To Disable this constraint, set the value to 0", but `0` doesn't disable either of them. Both problems only affect apps with `RegisterGenericHandlers = true`.

## `MaxGenericTypeRegistrations = 0` rejects every generic handler

`ServiceRegistrar.GenerateCombinations` checks this limit only when `MaxGenericTypeParameters > 0`, instead of when `MaxGenericTypeRegistrations > 0`:

```csharp
if (MaxGenericTypeParameters > 0 && totalCombinations > MaxGenericTypeRegistrations)
```

With the default `MaxGenericTypeParameters = 10`, setting `MaxGenericTypeRegistrations = 0` makes registration throw as soon as any generic handler is found:

```
System.ArgumentException : Error registering the generic type: . The total number of generic type registrations exceeds the maximum allowed (0).
```

Conversely, setting `MaxGenericTypeParameters = 0` also turns off the registrations limit, even when `MaxGenericTypeRegistrations` is set.

## `RegistrationTimeout = 0` times out immediately

`AddMediatRClassesWithTimeout` passes the value straight to `new CancellationTokenSource(RegistrationTimeout)`, and a delay of `0` cancels the token immediately. Registration then fails as soon as it reaches a generic handler:

```
System.TimeoutException : The generic handler registration process timed out.
```

## Fix

- Check the registrations limit only when `MaxGenericTypeRegistrations > 0`.
- Treat a `RegistrationTimeout` of `0` or less as no timeout.

Neither change can break an app that works today: with these values, registration currently always fails once any generic handler is found.

The docs at https://docs.mediatr.io/en/latest/Generic-requests-and-handlers.html currently describe the existing behavior, and need updating with the fix.
